# Contributing to git-coin

Thanks for helping. git-coin is a small price collector that runs on GitHub Actions (Node.js 24, TypeScript, no runtime dependencies). Keep changes **small and focused**; do not refactor code that the change does not need. The reasons behind the design are in the [decision records](../docs/adr/0000-index.md), and the module contracts are in [docs/implementation/plan.md](../docs/implementation/plan.md).

## Set up

Requirement: Node.js 24.22.1 (enforced by `engines` and `engine-strict`). If your default Node is another version, put `./scripts/with-node24.sh` in front of every npm and git command, for example `./scripts/with-node24.sh npm run check`.

```bash
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run prepare       # installs the Husky pre-commit hook in your clone
npm run check         # the gate for every change
```

## Checks to run before a pull request

`npm run check` runs everything below in this order. CI runs the same checks on every pull request.

| Command                  | What it checks                                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `npm run format:check`   | Prettier (`npm run format` fixes it)                   |
| `npm run check:versions` | Every dependency has an exact version (no `^`, no `~`) |
| `npm run lint`           | ESLint and the TypeScript 7 type check                 |
| `npm run lint:docs`      | Markdown lint and relative links                       |
| `npm run lint:unused`    | Unused files, exports and dependencies (knip)          |
| `npm test`               | `node --test` on `test/**/*.test.ts` (no network)      |

## Code and tests

- Follow the existing style: tabs, width 4, single quotes, trailing commas `es5`, and a block `if` with `return` (no one-line `if`). Prettier and ESLint enforce most of it.
- TypeScript runs natively on Node 24, so only erasable syntax is allowed: no `enum`, no `namespace`, no parameter properties. Use `import type` for types and `.ts` extensions in relative imports.
- No runtime dependencies. Use the built-in `fetch`, `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`.
- Prices are strings. They are written to the CSV exactly as the source gave them. Numbers are used only for comparisons and percentages.
- Modules import only `src/types.ts` and `src/time.ts` from each other, and only `src/collect.ts` wires them together. The shared types are a contract: change them in their own pull request and say why.
- Every behavior change comes with tests. Tests need no network: use a fake `HttpClient`, a local `node:http` server, or temp directories. Fixtures are synthetic, with made-up prices such as `100.00`. Never commit a raw response from a price source (some sources forbid it, see [ADR 0002](../docs/adr/0002-data-sources.md)).
- **Dependencies**: exact versions only. Install with `npm install -E <package>@latest` (add `-D` for a development dependency), then run `npm run check:versions`.
- **Workflows**: pin every action by full commit SHA with the version in a comment, give each job the smallest `permissions` it needs, and never put untrusted text into a `run:` line ([ADR 0009](../docs/adr/0009-security-reliability-testing.md)).
- **Secrets and personal data** never go into the repository.

## Add a coin or a source

- A coin is added in `config/coins.json`: see "Add a coin" in the [README](../README.md) and [ADR 0007](../docs/adr/0007-configuration-and-adding-coins.md). Fill the id of each stored source that lists the coin (at least one). Disable a coin instead of deleting it.
- A new source needs an adapter, tests with synthetic fixtures, and a look at its terms. Open a [feature request](https://github.com/borbiuk/git-coin/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) first.

## Documentation

Docs are written in simple English, and every command, path and value must match the code. Markdown is checked by markdownlint and by a relative-link check (`npm run lint:docs`). A change to an npm script, a module contract or a command also updates [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and the plan.

## Commits and pull requests

- A pull request title (it becomes the commit title) starts with an upper case letter, is written in the imperative mood ("Add the CSV writer"), has at most 72 characters, does not end with a period and has no `WIP`, `fixup!` or `squash!`. CI checks everything except the imperative mood ([check-pr-title.mjs](../scripts/check-pr-title.mjs)).
- One change per pull request. The maintainer pushes small changes straight to `main`; outside contributions come as pull requests.
- The Husky pre-commit hook runs `npm run format` and stages **every modified tracked file**, so partial commits do not work. New files must be added with `git add` yourself.
- No attribution lines: no `Co-Authored-By` trailer and no "generated by" text in commit messages, pull request descriptions or docs. Do not pass `--author` and do not change the git identity of the repository.
- Never push to `main` with `--force`. The `main` and `data` branches reject force pushes and deletion.

## Reporting

- Bugs and ideas: [issues](https://github.com/borbiuk/git-coin/issues). More in [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md).
- Security problems: **not** in a public issue, see [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).
- Everyone follows the [Code of Conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
